comparison: Both address claims about SIRT-1's deacetylase activity independence (C7, C43, C52, C53, C54). OpenEval finds the rescue experiments provide strong support, while peer review raises significant concerns about overexpression artifacts and notes that EX527 inhibitor data contradicts the conclusion, marking this as UNCERTAIN and requiring more investigation.

Both evaluate SIRT-1's proviral activity independence from autophagy (C8, C44, C81, C82). OpenEval and peer review agree this is SUPPORTED by ATG-7 KO experiments, with no challenges raised by reviewers.

Both address SIRT-1's role in ER stress pathway (C9, C42, C90, C91). OpenEval result R7 covers epistasis with thapsigargin, while R8 covers epistasis with SERCA2A. Peer review R3 accepts the ER stress mechanism as SUPPORTED without challenge, covering claims from both OpenEval results.

Both address genetic epistasis showing SIRT-1 acts through SERCA2A/ER stress (C10, C11, C92). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED by double knockdown data, and peer review accepts the mechanism without challenge.

Both evaluate EV-mediated release and SIRT-1's role (C15, C16, C123, C124, C134, C135, C163, C164). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED by EV fraction data. Peer review marks UNCERTAIN, requesting better vesicle characterization (isopycnic gradients, EM) and more complete temporal analysis beyond early timepoints.

Both address CD63-positive EV release (C129, C130, C156). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by western blot and immunofluorescence showing decreased extracellular CD63. Peer review marks UNCERTAIN, noting authors never demonstrate virus-loaded vesicles are actually CD63-positive (requesting CD63 pulldown experiments).

Both evaluate SIRT-1 translocation to cytoplasm during infection (C40, C56, C57, C60, C62). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by immunofluorescence and western blots. Peer review marks UNCERTAIN, questioning whether translocation is targeted export versus leaky nuclear pores, noting leptomycin-B control is not compelling and requesting quantitative fractionation.

Both address SIRT-1's role in poliovirus infection (C12, C45, C112, C113). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by consistent effects across genetic and pharmacological approaches. Peer review accepts this finding as SUPPORTED without challenge.

Both evaluate SIRT-1's role in SARS-CoV-2 infection (C13, C46, C120, C122, C191, C192). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, extending prior MERS-CoV work. Peer review accepts this as SUPPORTED without challenge.

Both address lack of SIRT-1 effect on CVB3 (C14, C47, C111, C114, C115, C197, C198). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED showing virus-specific differences. Peer review accepts this as SUPPORTED, demonstrating differential requirements across viruses.

Both address SIRT-1 knockdown effects on viral titers and autophagy induction (C5, C6, C70, C74). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by differential effects on extracellular vs intracellular titers and autophagy markers. Peer review accepts these findings as SUPPORTED without challenge.

OpenEval R28 addresses the apparent contradiction about deacetylase activity requirements (C187, C188, C189), marking it UNCERTAIN. Peer review R1 also questions deacetylase independence (C140, C188, C189), noting EX527 data suggests activity may be required, marking UNCERTAIN.

OpenEval R21 integrates evidence for autophagy-independent mechanism (C139, C140, C141). Peer review R2 accepts autophagy independence (C139) as SUPPORTED, though this is part of their broader acceptance of the ATG-7 KO data.

OpenEval R4 addresses control experiments ruling out nuclear leakage (C60, C61, C62). Peer review R6 questions this interpretation (C60, C62), noting the leptomycin-B control is not compelling and marking UNCERTAIN.

OpenEval R17 integrates multiple lines of evidence for the mechanistic model including EV release (C17, C41, C131, C152). Peer review R4 questions the EV characterization aspects (C41 relates to mechanism), marking UNCERTAIN due to insufficient vesicle characterization.

OpenEval finds autophagy induction by SIRT-1 knockdown (C70, C74, C66-C73) SUPPORTED by western blot and immunofluorescence. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though peer R10 accepts related autophagy findings.

OpenEval finds SERCA2A stability requires SIRT-1 deacetylase activity (C94, C95, C96, C173) SUPPORTED by differential rescue experiments. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though this relates to the deacetylase activity controversy in peer R1.
OpenEval finds virus suppresses ER stress markers (C98, C99, C183, C184) SUPPORTED by western blot data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval finds effects consistent across cell types including primary airway cells (C100-C109) SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval finds negative controls ruling out effects on replication, binding, entry (C149, C150, C151, C142) SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval finds autophagy role in EV-D68 release and SIRT-1 colocalization (C77-C80) SUPPORTED by immunofluorescence and titer data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval finds rapid SIRT-1 translocation without p62 colocalization (C144-C148) SUPPORTED, suggesting regulatory role rather than substrate. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval finds epistasis analysis supports ER stress mechanism (C167, C168, C178-C182) SUPPORTED, though ER stress induction hypothesis needs validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer R3 accepts the ER stress mechanism generally.
OpenEval marks generalization to 'many betacoronaviruses' (C193, C206) as UNCERTAIN, requiring testing additional viruses. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval finds virus-specific differences in SIRT-1 requirements (C118, C138, C200-C203) SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers accept differential effects across viruses in R7, R8, R9.
OpenEval finds background claims about EV-D68 epidemiology (C2, C3, C4) SUPPORTED by prior literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval finds extensive background claims (C18-C39) about SIRT-1, autophagy, ER stress SUPPORTED by prior literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval marks generalization about enterovirus ER stress suppression strategy (C185, C186) as UNCERTAIN, requiring additional viruses and mechanistic understanding. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval finds hypothesis about impaired EV biogenesis/release (C126) SUPPORTED by combined intracellular/extracellular CD63 data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer R5 questions whether vesicles are actually CD63-positive.
OpenEval finds increased CD63 in EVs from infected cells (C155) SUPPORTED by western blot. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval marks therapeutic potential claim (C207) as UNCERTAIN, noting feasibility remains to be demonstrated. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
